stemMd: A manager argues that an organization should retain redundant communication channels, as a ship retains lifeboats even when its main hull is sound. Which feature is most important to the analogy?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A backup can be worth maintaining even when it is rarely needed in normal operation.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Ships and organizations both have leaders.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Lifeboats and communication channels cost exactly the same.

explanationMd: The relevant similarity is protection against a low-frequency but consequential failure. Normal reliability of the main system does not eliminate the value of a fallback. Literal physical resemblance is unnecessary.

distractorRationale.c: Physical resemblance is irrelevant to the functional analogy.
distractorRationale.b: The analogy specifically concerns infrequent emergency use.
distractorRationale.d: Leadership is not the reason for keeping the backup.
distractorRationale.e: Equal costs are unnecessary and implausible.
